item.title: Openness, innovation and cooperation urged
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
President Xi Jinping highlighted on Wednesday the emergence of Shenzhen, Guangdong province, the host city of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting, from a fishing village to a metropolitan city, saying that the story of Shenzhen is a microcosm of China's reform and opening-up and a shining example of Asia-Pacific cooperation. Xi made the remarks in a speech delivered at the banquet that he and his wife, Peng Liyuan, hosted to welcome guests attending the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting. "I have often said that to see over a few thousand years of China, go to Xi'an; to see 500 years of China, go to Beijing; to see 100 years of China, go to Shanghai. Tonight, let me add this: To see 50 years of China, come to Shenzhen," he said, adding that Shenzhen is a place with a big story to tell. Xi recalled that in 1978, when he first visited Shenzhen, it was still a small fishing village. More than 40 years have passed, and the city is filled with high-rises and bustling traffic — a transformation nothing short of miraculous, he said. Xi highlighted that openness is in Shenzhen's DNA, innovation is the wellspring of its vitality and cooperation is the source of its strength. Growing from attracting foreign investment and technology to actively shaping the international rules, Shenzhen today has trade links spanning the globe and welcomes an endless stream of businesspeople and travelers, serving as a window of high-standard opening-up in China, he said. Xi noted that Shenzhen has developed from a city of export processing to an independent research and development hub, and from being the "world factory" to becoming a "city of innovation". Today's Shenzhen files up to 20,000 international patent applications annually, with advanced manufacturing and modern service industries thriving side by side, placing it at the forefront of cluster-based innovation in China, he said. He highlighted the inclusiveness of the city and quoted the people of Shenzhen as saying, "Once here, Shenzhener forever." The city opens its minds and arms to go-getters from around the world and brings together talent from over 100 countries and regions, making it a vibrant hub of win-win cooperation between China and the rest of the world, Xi said. He emphasized that since its founding, APEC has been marked by openness, innovation and cooperation. From the first handshake in Seattle, the United States, to the historic gathering by Beijing's Yanqi Lake, and from the solemn commitment to the Bogor Goals to the broad vision of building an Asia-Pacific community — APEC has remained attuned to the pulse of the times, spearheaded economic integration in the Asia-Pacific region, and helped to make the region the most dynamic in the global economy and a vital engine of world growth, Xi said. Xi noted that since becoming the APEC chair, China has hosted more than 300 meetings and events across 16 cities in the course of the year. He commended the active participation of the member economies, saying that they have contributed to significant outcomes during the APEC China Year. He expressed his expectation for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting to be a venue to discuss steps to expand mutual openness, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, extend opportunities for result-oriented cooperation across various fields, and strive to deliver more tangible results on the ground. "I look forward to discussing with you the great endeavor of Asia-Pacific cooperation and advancing our shared cause of Asia-Pacific development," he said. After the banquet, Xi and Peng, along with the guests, watched a cultural performance.

item.title: President invites global firms to share in China’s development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
President Xi Jinping invited businesses worldwide on Wednesday to share in China's development, pledging to open its vast market further, create more opportunities for companies to innovate and grow, and offer investors a more stable and predictable business environment. Xi made the remarks when delivering a keynote speech at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province. Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and representatives of 115 Fortune Global 500 companies were among those attending. Describing Asia-Pacific business communities as "pioneers of the global economy", Xi encouraged business leaders to take an active part in China's reform and opening-up and to "share in the opportunities created by Chinese modernization". Xi said that China, the world's second-largest consumer market, offers businesses new opportunities in areas ranging from new energy vehicles to smart homes and from goods and services for older consumers to winter tourism. As China accelerates the development of a big, open market and increases imports of quality products and services, more diverse demand will be unleashed, he said. He also said that China will continue to host the "Export to China" series and other events to open efficient channels to help quality products from across the world enter the Chinese market. China is a supersized innovation testing ground where frontier technologies are tested, improved and upgraded in real-world scenarios and are then turned into high-quality growth drivers, Xi said. He pointed to robots at work in factories and on farms, autonomous driving and drone delivery as examples of how companies are putting new technologies to use. Xi said that China will deepen integration between technological and industrial innovation, and support the transformation and upgrading of traditional industries, the expansion of emerging industries and the forward-looking planning of industries of the future. Xi said China will provide global business communities with an environment that enables mutually reinforcing cooperation. In the face of unilateralism and protectionism, China has remained committed to true multilateralism, and has steadily brought stability and predictability to world economic growth and international trade and economic cooperation. "No matter how the international landscape may evolve, China will not waver in its pursuit of win-win cooperation with all other countries," he said. China will not only cut tariffs and expand market access, but will also go a step further by carrying out reform in challenging areas, such as rules, regulations and standards, Xi said. It will allow full manufacturing access with an accommodating business climate and steadily expand opening-up in the services sector, he said. For Annette Gregg, CEO of the World Trade Centers Association, the message from Xi's speech to companies is clear. "If you want to do business with China, China is open to you and ready for your business," she said. Gregg said that China's advances in robotics, artificial intelligence and green technology hold particular appeal for the United States market. Ramon Jara, a director of Chile's Antofagasta Minerals, welcomed Xi's invitation. "It's very good news for all of us trying to jointly develop the future of this region," he said. The two-day CEO summit launched the Shenzhen Initiative on Wednesday, marking the first time in its 30-year history that it has published an outcome document in the form of an initiative. China is hosting APEC for the third time, having previously hosted the leaders' meeting in Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. Xi will chair the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting on Thursday. In his address on Wednesday to the CEO summit, Xi said that China is ready to work with other economies to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community and bring prosperity for all in the region. "Today, we find ourselves in a changing and turbulent world," Xi said, noting the lack of momentum in global growth and rampant unilateralism and protectionism. "Still, global trade keeps growing against headwinds, and breakthroughs are being made in emerging technologies at a faster pace, exerting a profound impact on global development," he said. To bring prosperity for all in the Asia-Pacific region, Xi called for efforts to uphold peace and stability, build bridges for opening-up and cooperation, boost innovation to drive growth, and expand ways for mutual benefit and win-win outcomes. "There can be no prosperity without security, and no security without stability," Xi said. He urged economies to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation and overcome challenges through solidarity and cooperation. "History tells us that opening doors brings progress while closing doors leaves one behind," he said, calling for steady progress toward a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific. Founded in 1989, APEC now comprises 21 economies that together accounted for 61.6 percent of global real GDP, 50.1 percent of the world's total exports of goods and 48.5 percent of world total imports of goods in 2025, according to APEC figures. Xi urged APEC members to forge science, technology and innovation partnerships, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and AI, and promote green and low-carbon transition. He also called on members to remove trade and investment barriers to build an open Asia-Pacific economy, while promoting development that is balanced and delivers benefits to all to ensure both efficiency and fairness. Noting that Shenzhen is part of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, Xi said China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas across the world. Jeffrey Sachs, director of the Center for Sustainable Development at Columbia University in the US, said: "I believe in China's leadership in the next phase of green and digital development. Shenzhen is the world-leading cluster of innovation." He said that China wants an open, peaceful world environment where everybody can prosper, and China sees trade and investment as a path to shared prosperity. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Why ASEAN integration matters for the Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
As Asia-Pacific leaders prepare to gather in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov 18-19, they face a region that is more economically integrated than ever, yet increasingly vulnerable to fragmentation. While businesses depend on cross-border production networks, governments continue to impose trade restrictions and measures to protect domestic industries. This tension between economic interconnectedness and policy fragmentation has become a challenge for regional cooperation. China's APEC 2026 theme, "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together", emphasizes openness, innovation and cooperation — priorities that are both timely and crucial. The State of Southeast Asia 2026 Survey by the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute also reflects these priorities. When asked how the Association of Southeast Asian Nations should strengthen its resilience and relevance, 28.5 percent of the respondents favored increasing intra-regional trade and investment, while 20.7 percent supported diversifying supply chains to cushion economic tensions. In the face of rising protectionism and nationalism, the largest group of respondents favored accelerating regional integration. These findings suggest that ASEAN's preferred strategy against growing economic uncertainty is to strengthen internal economic ties while maintaining open partnerships beyond the region. Greater integration can create more opportunities within ASEAN, fortify supply chains, and make the region less vulnerable to external shocks. The survey also reveals a less discussed problem: 30.2 percent of the respondents identified limited domestic technocratic capacity to implement regional initiatives and 30.1 percent felt development disparities among member states were the leading impediments to intra-regional economic cooperation. Geopolitical pressures, while important, ranked behind these internal constraints. ASEAN has adopted numerous economic agreements and initiatives, but their effectiveness hinges on national-level implementation. Differences in regulatory capacity, infrastructure and digital readiness can hinder progress. The question is not whether ASEAN has sufficient instruments, but whether businesses, particularly micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, can practically benefit from these agreements. Singapore's 2027 ASEAN Chairmanship is an opportunity to advance this agenda. Singapore has prioritized deeper integration and stronger external partnerships. Achieving these goals would help ASEAN attract investment, expand partnerships beyond the region and strengthen its role in regional supply chains. To advance regional integration, ASEAN must address practical barriers to cross-border trade, including cumbersome customs procedures, inefficient logistics and differences in regulatory criteria. Greater technical cooperation and capability enhancement would also help less-developed member states implement regional commitments, enabling businesses, particularly MSMEs, to benefit more fully from regional integration. These efforts matter even more as companies adjust their supply chains to manage geopolitical and economic risks. China's manufacturing and technological strengths complement ASEAN's growing markets and production bases, alongside Singapore's role in logistics and financial services. The challenge is to maintain these economic ties while allowing businesses to diversify production and sourcing — without creating new trade barriers or dividing the region into competing economic blocs. Beyond trade in goods, digital integration is increasingly important. ASEAN's Digital Economy Framework Agreement, whose negotiations concluded in 2026, aims to facilitate digital trade and improve interoperability. If implemented effectively, it could reduce transaction costs and help smaller companies access regional markets through electronic documentation, digital payments and more compatible systems. The challenge will be to ensure that differences in national regulations and digital capabilities do not create new barriers. APEC plays a different but complementary role. While ASEAN advances integration through regional commitments, APEC brings together a broader group of economies for voluntary cooperation. It can promote trade facilitation, supply-chain connectivity, and compatible digital standards, even when members disagree on broader trade policy. The goal is not to establish identical rules, but to reduce unnecessary friction across markets. As the current APEC host and a major economic partner of ASEAN, China has a significant role to play. Economic cooperation will be judged by the sustainability and mutual benefits it delivers. The wider rules-based multilateral trading system, centered on the World Trade Organization, remains just as important. Smaller economies, in particular, rely on predictable rules rather than bargaining power alone. Regional arrangements should reinforce this system, not replace it. Although WTO reform remains difficult, Asia-Pacific economies share an interest in preserving common trade rules and preventing further fragmentation. Stronger ASEAN integration therefore matters beyond Southeast Asia. It can make regional production networks more resilient, sustain open partnerships and support wider Asia-Pacific cooperation. In a world of increasing protectionism, the priority should be to make existing frameworks deliver more effectively for businesses and communities, while preserving the common rules which support regional prosperity. The author is the former head of the External Relations Division of the ASEAN Secretariat and a senior fellow and coordinator at the ASEAN Studies Centre in the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute. The views don't necessarily reflect those of China Daily. If you have a specific expertise, or would like to share your thought about our stories, then send us your writings at opinion@chinadaily.com.cn, and comment@chinadaily.com.cn.

item.title: In conversation with Cui Tiankai: US domestic noise should not derail China-US ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Before heading to Shenzhen to cover the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, we attended the US-China Political Dialogue 2026 held in Beijing. There, we spoke with Cui Tiankai, former Chinese ambassador to the US, about the key issues shaping China-US relations. Here are some of his key quotes from the interview: • The US ought to focus on fixing its own problems, rather than always looking elsewhere. • There are various noises and events inside the US. Some have absolutely nothing to do with China and shouldn't derail China-US ties. • The Pacific is vast enough for China and the US to grow together, and for the whole Asia-Pacific to thrive side by side. If the US joins us [China] and regional nations in this endeavor, we can achieve so much.

item.title: Regional development, connectivity stressed
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Editor's note: President Xi Jinping held six bilateral talks with leaders attending the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on Tuesday. President Xi Jinping called on Tuesday for China and Vietnam to enhance mutual trust and solidarity, deepen comprehensive cooperation, and jointly safeguard peace and stability and promote development and prosperity. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks during a meeting with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam in Shenzhen. He described China and Vietnam as "comrades and brothers", saying that "the rougher the seas, the more we must pull together". While calling for promoting the alignment of their interests, Xi underlined the need for both countries to boost connectivity, advance the early establishment of smart ports and cross-border economic cooperation zones, expand collaboration in digital transformation and green, low-carbon development, and explore partnership in applications of artificial intelligence. He called on both sides to properly manage their differences in the South China Sea issue, steadily advance maritime cooperation, and strengthen cooperation within frameworks such as the United Nations, China-ASEAN cooperation, and Lancang-Mekong cooperation. Xi also expressed China's willingness to strengthen mutual learning with Vietnam in development experiences, firmly support each other, and deepen exchanges on party self-supervision and self-governance. To Lam expressed his congratulations on the successful convening of the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee. He said that Vietnam highly values its relationship with China, and regards it as its most important strategic partner. In the current complex international situation, Vietnam is willing to strengthen solidarity and cooperation with China to aid each other's development, he added. caodesheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi calls for advancing steady, sound development of China-ROK relations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called for advancing the steady and sound development of relations between China and the Republic of Korea (ROK) as next year marks the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two "friendly neighbors and strategic cooperative partners." Xi made the remarks during his meeting with ROK President Lee Jae Myung, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov 18-19. The two countries should uphold strategic independence, maintain the political foundation for bilateral relations, and further consolidate and develop the relationship, Xi stressed. China and the ROK have substantially concluded the second phase of negotiations on the China-ROK Free Trade Agreement. The two countries should make full use of this institutional arrangement to strengthen macroeconomic policy coordination and foster a collaborative ecosystem for emerging technology industries such as artificial intelligence, Xi said. China also stands ready to work with the ROK to facilitate people-to-people exchanges and carry out sound and beneficial cultural exchanges in a step-by-step manner, Xi said. The two sides should further strengthen multilateral coordination, jointly uphold true multilateralism, advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community and the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, make greater contributions to regional peace and development, and maintain the stability and smooth functioning of global industrial and supply chains, Xi said. For his part, Lee said that the two countries have seen sustained momentum in the comprehensive restoration of ROK-China relations, with bilateral economic and trade cooperation growing rapidly, people-to-people exchanges becoming increasingly frequent, and mutual perceptions steadily improving. The ROK's commitment to the one-China principle has not changed and will not change, Lee stressed. The ROK hopes to maintain close high-level exchanges with China, strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, and industrial and supply chains, foster closer people-to-people bonds, and pursue a more mature ROK-China strategic partnership, he said.

item.title: Xi says China-Russia relations bring stability, certainty to turbulent world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping said Wednesday that China-Russia relations have brought greater stability and certainty to a world of turbulence and transformation. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov 18-19. Xi noted that this year marks the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation. He said that China-Russia ties set an example for a new model of major-country relations featuring equality, mutual respect, good faith, and win-win cooperation. Xi called on both countries to deepen all-round cooperation and firmly uphold the due responsibilities and obligations of major countries to guide and promote a multipolar world and democratization of international relations. Both sides should leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between their governments, legislatures, militaries and political parties to ensure that the consensus reached by the two heads of state is effectively implemented, Xi said. Xi called on the two countries to provide a more stable and predictable investment and business environment and protect the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises from both countries. The development of China and Russia is closely intertwined with that of the Asia-Pacific region, and APEC is an important platform for enhancing cooperation, Xi noted. China stands ready to work with the Asia-Pacific family, including Russia, to chart a course for the region's prosperity and development and build an Asia-Pacific community together, Xi said. Putin said he and Xi have held four productive meetings so far this year, helping sustain the sound development momentum in Russia-China relations. High-level exchanges have been close, bilateral trade has reached a new high, and practical cooperation has made substantial progress across various fields, he said. Russia is willing to strengthen back-to-back strategic coordination with China, expand cooperation in trade, energy, education and other fields, and broaden cultural and people-to-people exchanges to better benefit the two peoples, Putin said. Russia also stands ready to work with China to promote development and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, advance the process toward a multipolar world and build a more just and equitable global governance system, he added.

item.title: Xi welcomes Trump at Shenzhen airport
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping on Wednesday welcomed US President Donald Trump at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in South China's Guangdong province. Trump is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov 18-19. Amid welcome music, Xi and Trump shook hands warmly. Honor guards of the Chinese People's Liberation Army presented arms to salute, and a girl handed the US leader a bouquet. The national flags of China and the United States fluttered in the wind as a military band played the national anthems of the two countries, and fighter jets flew overhead in salute. The two heads of state waved to a welcoming young crowd. Xi recalled his state visit to the United States in September this year, when the US presidential couple came to the airport in person and hosted a grand welcoming ceremony, noting that China is a nation with a tradition of courtesy that values reciprocating goodwill.
